title: PostgreSQL: more connections, less throughput
question: What happens when a traffic spike makes the API open hundreds of connections straight to the database?
description: The API calls PostgreSQL directly, one connection per request, with max_connections at 300. The database peaks at about 44 active connections; beyond that every query gets slower as they fight over locks and buffers. From 20 to 30 seconds traffic rises from 1,400 to 2,400 requests per second.
assumptions: Abstract request-level model: no TCP, TLS, packets or real HTTP proxy semantics.
Each component has fixed concurrency slots and a FIFO queue; there is no CPU, memory or GC model.
Components do not know when their caller gave up, unless deadline propagation is on.
Numbers are scenario inputs, not measured performance of any product.
Database slowdown under many active connections follows the Universal Scalability Law with illustrative coefficients (contention 0.02, coherency 0.0005), not measured PostgreSQL numbers.
expectedObservations: Once the spike arrives, active connections climb into the hundreds and every query becomes several times slower.
Database throughput drops below normal traffic, so the system does not recover even after the spike is over.
